subject: Demo recap + proposed POC plan - Enterprisefin
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
To: Oliver Hayes <oliver.hayes@enterprisefin.com>, Sana Patel <sana.patel@enterprisefin.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Mar 2028 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Demo recap + proposed POC plan - Enterprisefin

Hi Oliver / Sana —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Great conversation — appreciate the clarity on your primary success criteria. Per our demo and discussion, I've summarized the proposed 4-week POC plan below and included the evaluation criteria we recommend focusing on.

High-level goals (what success looks like)
- Accuracy: Redwood-generated responses match or exceed your current template QA pass rate (target: >= 92% on the 500-sample test set)
- Latency: 95th percentile latency under 450ms for typical request size (avg ~300 tokens)
- Cost: Per-request token cost reduction compared to existing vendor (target: <= 70% of current TCO)
- Integration: Ability to route specific customer segments to dedicated model variant with no production incidents for 2 weeks

Proposed POC scope & plan (4 weeks)
Week 0 (kickoff) — alignment on endpoints, test data, and access: Redwood will get a sandbox API key and examples; Enterprisefin provides anonymized sample payloads and the 500-sample evaluation set.
Week 1 — integration & baseline: Integrate Redwood SDK to dev environment; run baseline comparisons against current vendor; collect latency/throughput metrics.
Week 2 — tuning & instrumentation: Apply recommended batching/quantization profile; iterate on prompts and routing policy; instrument tracing and cost metrics.
Week 3 — validation & handoff: Run the formal evaluation (500-sample pass/fail, latency distribution, cost report); review findings and next steps for production rollout.

Ownership
- Enterprisefin: Provide evaluation set, sandbox environment access, and a single technical contact for integrations (Oliver / Sana).
- Redwood: Provide SRE contact, SE support (Dylan), recommended config, and the evaluation report.

Deliverables
- Redwood: POC SOW (attached), access to sandbox, weekly status notes, final evaluation report (metrics + recommendations)
- Enterprisefin: Sample dataset, test keys, and decision by end of week 4

Attachments: Redwood_POC_SOW_Enterprisefin_v1.pdf, evaluation-metrics.xlsx

Next steps
1) Can you confirm the sandbox IP allowlist and who will be the technical point of contact on your side?
2) If that looks good, we'll kick off next Monday (Mar 20) and schedule a 30-min kickoff with Dylan and your tech lead.

Thanks — happy to adjust timelines if you need a different cadence.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com
(415) 555-0134

Thanks Marissa — this is very helpful. Quick answers and a couple of clarifications: 

- Sandbox allowlist: procurement needs the IP block + SOC2 attachments before they'll approve. I'll loop them in next. For immediate work, we can use our dev environment keys (non-prod) if you prefer.
- Technical lead: I'll be the primary contact, Sana will own data transfer and anonymization. I'll also bring in our infra lead (cc'd in the next thread) if we need firewall changes.
- Success criteria: the accuracy target makes sense; on latency, our internal SLA for the customer-facing endpoint is 400ms p95. Can Redwood confidentally hit <= 400ms if we use the dedicated variant you showed?

We're keen to get started — can you do the kickoff Monday Mar 20 at 10am PT? Also please share the SOW and the evaluation spreadsheet in Drive (I saw they're attached to this thread).

Thanks,
Oliver
Director, Product
Enterprisefin
